answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with staked, non-transferable identity. Each agent locks collateral and signs every vote with a private cipher key; the ledger spots a clone that votes twice and slashes its bond. Reputation only reaches its zenith after long honest service and cannot be bought or split, so a fake army needs fresh capital per persona. Honest work earns the network's nectar, but an attacker must stake real value for every fake identity and forfeits it when caught, making mass impersonation costly rather than free.
